prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Build a single-file landing page for Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930) that uses only the facts in FACTSHEET.md and links to its source.

[action]
- Wrote `landing/index.html`. It has no build step. The only external request is Google Fonts (Archivo / Archivo Black), and it falls back to system sans-serif if that fails.
- Every section is a CSS grid with 14px black gaps on a black page, so the whole layout reads as Mondrian black lines. The panels use only red, blue, yellow, white, grey and black.
- The hero has a schematic of the painting built from the fact sheet's description: a large red square top right, a small blue square bottom left and a small yellow rectangle bottom right, on white with black lines. A text alternative describes it for screen readers.
- Sections, in order: title and alternate title; painter, year (with medium), movement and collection; the Neoplasticism rules; the picture; why it matters; and a "Read more on Wikipedia" link to the fact sheet's URL.
- Assumptions:
  - I did not use three.js. Flat planes suit this subject better, and the page has one less thing that can fail.
  - The schematic's proportions are my own, because the fact sheet gives none. The footer says it is a schematic, not a reproduction.
  - On screens 760px wide or narrower, the sections stack into one column.

[result]
- The page text only restates fact sheet lines; I wrote it from them directly. The only additions are the footer note about the illustration and the label "Wikipedia" on the link to the source URL.
- I traced the layout of the painting graphic by hand: every grid cell is filled and the red, blue and yellow blocks land where the fact sheet puts them.
- `grep -c "1930" landing/index.html` returned `4`, which only confirms the year appears.
- Not checked: I did not open the page in a browser, so how it actually looks is unconfirmed. I opened no browser tabs, so there was nothing to close.

[next] Open `landing/index.html` in a browser to check the layout at desktop and phone widths.
